_what: Circuit parameters for the spiking basal-ganglia-thalamus selection loop (synth/basal_ganglia.py, Stage 26). Every number is labelled MEASURED/MODEL (taken from the cited paper), ASSUMED (our choice, stated), or FITTED (set by a scan in this project, see results/bg/*).

primary_source.citation: Humphries MD, Stewart RD, Gurney KN (2006) A physiologically plausible model of action selection and oscillatory activity in the basal ganglia. J Neurosci 26(50):12921-12942. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.3486-06.2006; ModelDB 83559 (MATLAB).
primary_source.what_we_took: populations, pathways, within/between-channel connection probabilities, delays, PSP sizes and time constants, membrane constants, tonic currents, reset/refractory/noise, selection criterion, switching protocol

per_channel_n.label: MODEL
per_channel_n.note: Humphries 2006: 3 channels x 64 neurons per population; we keep 64 per channel for K channels

neuron_model.equation: LIF, v relative to rest: tau_m dv/dt = -v + R*I_spon + PSP currents; reset 0 mV; refractory 2 ms; Gaussian noise SD 0.3 mV; lower bound v >= -V_lim (chloride reversal)
neuron_model.label: MODEL

D1.note: I_down = 0.25 nA hyperpolarising (striatal down state held as a constant current)

Thal.drive_mV: 24 ASSUMED starting value; thal_gain FITTED in the learner (results/bg/learn_*.json)
Thal.label: ASSUMED generic relay cell; SNr holds it near silence at rest

neuron_model._tonic_currents_note: Humphries 2006 tuned its tonic currents to hit the recorded rates with its own cortical input; we did the same for ours (stand-in cortex at 3 spikes/s background, ctx_gain 2.0, ctx_gain_stn 0.3): STN 1.22 nA, GP 0.38 nA, SNr 0.42 nA give STN 10.2, GP 18.8, SNr 25.3 Hz (all inside the ranges below); D2 stays silent at rest (0.0 Hz, floor 0.01 Hz) — a stated residual.

synapses.label: MODEL
synapses.kernel: exponential current, scaled so one spike gives the stated peak PSP on the target membrane

striatal_output_weight.note: D1->SNr and D2->GP carry weight 4 (Oorschot 1996 cell counts); all others 1

connectivity.label: MODEL
connectivity.diffuse_p: 0.25 / K (Humphries: b = c/N = 0.083 for N = 3 channels); used for STN->GP, STN->SNr, GP->GP, SNr->SNr

pathways.type: conductance onto the dendrite (g_ed), weight = the column's external (thalamic) synapse for L5E x thal_gain
pathways.label: ASSUMED pathway, thal_gain FITTED

connectivity.cortical_input_note: Humphries 2006 drives each channel with Poisson 'salience' trains (4-40 spikes/s; 3 spikes/s background); the number of inputs per neuron is not stated in the paper. Here the input is the spikes of the cortical action pool (L5 pyramids of 9/46d), connected with probability ctx_p; the per-spike cortical PSP is scaled by ctx_gain (FITTED, results/bg/ctx_scan.json) because a pool of ~30-60 real cells at 3-20 Hz is not the same drive as the paper's salience trains.

left_out_in_this_version: dopamine modulation of cortico-striatal, STN and GP efficacy (paper: lambda_D1 = lambda_D2 = 0.3 normal)
striatal up/down-state dynamics beyond the constant I_down (paper: ~16 Hz striatal low-pass)
striatal fast-spiking interneurons, GP->striatum, thalamic reticular nucleus
reward prediction inside the circuit: the reward signal is still applied by the learner (external)

selection_criterion.label: MODEL
selection_criterion.rule: channel k is selected when its mean SNr rate falls below 5 spikes/s

switching_protocol.label: MODEL
switching_protocol.rule: channel 1 input from t = 1 s, channel 2 from t = 2.5 s, end 5 s; inputs 4..40 spikes/s in steps of 4 (100 pairs); switching = channel 1 selected during its input alone, then deselected and channel 2 selected

rate_targets_hz._note: awake or in vivo rodent, control animals; ranges span the cited means

sources: Kita & Kita 2011 (control rat striatal projection neurons: most very low, bursty ones < 2 Hz average)
Lindahl et al. 2013 Front Comput Neurosci 7:76 (basal MSN 0.01-2.0 Hz)
Humphries 2006 tuned STN to Kreiss et al. 1997; awake monkey 10-30 Hz (DeLong et al. 1985, via Bevan & Wilson 1999)
Urbain et al. 2000 Eur J Neurosci 12:3361 (32 Hz, awake head-restrained rat)
Ni et al. 2000 Eur J Neurosci 12:4338 (22.1 +/- 1.4 Hz, normal rat)
Humphries 2006 tuned SNr to Windels & Kiyatkin 2004

Thal.note: no reference range used in this version; the relay is a stand-in whose job is to be quiet under tonic SNr and to fire when its SNr channel drops below 5 Hz

ctx_gain.label: FITTED
ctx_gain.how: stand-in scan results/bg/scan_g*_s*.json: selection threshold 8 spikes/s (1.5 gives 12, the paper's circuit selects from ~10); in the learner the pools fire 4-6 spikes/s so 2.0 is the lowest gain at which the loop engages

ctx_gain_stn.label: FITTED
ctx_gain_stn.how: same scan; at 1.0 the hyperdirect STN burst (90-100 spikes/s) outweighs the direct pathway and no channel is ever selected

thal_gain.label: FITTED in the learner
thal_gain.how: the thalamo-cortical feedback is the one pathway with no measured weight here; too strong and the loop locks onto one pool between trials

cortico_striatal_plasticity._what: Stage 27: cue/context cells -> D1 and D2 of every channel, plastic; pool -> striatum channel wiring fixed
cortico_striatal_plasticity.rule: three-factor: eligibility from pre->post coincidences (pre trace tau_x) decaying with tau_e; at the dopamine signal delta: D1 weights += eta delta e, D2 weights -= eta delta e; weights clipped to [0, w_max_factor x initial]
sources: Reynolds JN, Hyland BI, Wickens JR (2001) A cellular mechanism of reward-related learning. Nature 413:67-70 (dopamine-dependent cortico-striatal potentiation)

Shen W, Flajolet M, Greengard P, Surmeier DJ (2008) Dichotomous dopaminergic control of striatal synaptic plasticity. Science 321:848-851 (D1 MSNs: LTP with dopamine; D2 MSNs: LTD with dopamine, LTP without)
Yagishita S et al. (2014) A critical time window for dopamine actions on the structural plasticity of dendritic spines. Science 345:1616-1620 (dopamine must follow the input within 0.3-2 s)
Pawlak V, Kerr JND (2008) Dopamine receptor activation is required for corticostriatal spike-timing-dependent plasticity. J Neurosci 28:2435-2446 (STDP windows of tens of ms)

cue_n_in.label: ASSUMED: same convergence as the pool input

ctx_gain_cue.label: FITTED (results/bg/plastic_*.json): the cue cells fire ~6 spikes/s during a cue, the stand-in's salience trains 30

dopamine_system._what: Stage 27b: SNc/VTA population, primary-reward input, negative-outcome input, striosomal critic; its rate deviation after the outcome is the prediction error that gates the plasticity

sources: Grace AA, Bunney BS (1984) The control of firing pattern in nigral dopamine neurons: single spike firing. J Neurosci 4:2866-2876
Schultz W (1998) Predictive reward signal of dopamine neurons. J Neurophysiol 80:1-27

phasic_burst.value: 15-30 spikes/s for 100-200 ms to unpredicted reward; pause on omission
sources: Bayer HM, Glimcher PW (2005) Neuron 47:129-141 (bursts encode positive errors linearly; dips are rate-floored)
Bayer, Lau & Glimcher (2007) J Neurophysiol 98:1428 (pause duration encodes negative errors)

reward_pathway.value: PPTg / lateral hypothalamus glutamate -> dopamine neurons
sources: Watabe-Uchida M, Eshel N, Uchida N (2017) Annu Rev Neurosci 40:373-394 (review of inputs)

critic_pathway.value: striosomal D1 MSNs -> SNc dopamine cells (GABA)
sources: Crittenden JR et al. (2016) Striosome-dendron bouquets, PNAS 113:11318
Houk JC, Adams JL, Barto AG (1995) model of how the basal ganglia generate and use neural signals that predict reinforcement

stand_ins_stated: LIF constants of the dopamine cells (tau 20 ms, theta 20 mV, refractory 10 ms) and the tonic drive (14.5 mV, FITTED to 4.5 spikes/s)
reward / habenula inputs as Poisson fibres (100 each, p 0.25, 10 spikes/s per unit outcome for 150 ms; FITTED to a 25-28 spikes/s burst and a pause to ~0)

the critic's inhibition onto dopamine cells decays with 500 ms so that a prediction formed during the cue still acts at the outcome 300-500 ms later: a stand-in for the temporal-difference circuit; the burst does not transfer to the cue here, and dopamine cells pause during a predictive cue, which is wrong-signed and unused
critic cells have the D1 membrane plus a per-cell resting offset uniform in [-15, 0] mV (ASSUMED heterogeneity) so the population's output is graded
delta = (rate - tonic) / 20 spikes/s, negative values x 4 (ASSUMED, so a full pause weighs as much as a full burst; the biology's asymmetry is in the references above)
